svg.text: Stateless hash-based signature: a PORS+FP few-time key, a 5-layer hypertree, target-sum WOTS. n = 16 B, P = 0.
Forced pruning: the signer grinds ρ until the 15 opened leaves need ≤ 120 authentication nodes · cached height-11 top tree · paired PRF secrets.
Layer 0 is the top of the hypertree (signs the public key); layer 4 is the bottom (signs the PORS root). Verification walks 4 → 0.
secrets sorted by leaf index; slot i = the i-th node the stack machine folds; slots after the octopus must be 0
Layer 1 shown: LE32 counter c + 42 WOTS chain values + h siblings = 676 + 16h B
THE 256-BIT MESSAGE DIGEST PICKS EVERY PATH
N = H(tw₁₂ ‖ P ‖ ρ ‖ 0¹²⁸ ‖ m), all 256 bits
one 64-byte block after the input format · read little-endian
Admissible iff the 15 leaf indices are distinct and their octopus has ≤ 120 nodes:
p ≈ 2⁻⁹·⁷⁶ (exact count), so the signer tries ≈ 870 randomizers ρ (a < 2²⁰). The verifier
enforces the same condition through its stack machine. Example: idx = 11,956,472,188, octopus = 114.
v_r = bits 34 + 14r … 47 + 14r: leaf of the PORS tree of idx (14 bits each)
e_L = leaf index in the layer-L tree (h_L bits: 11 for layer 0, 6 for layers 1–3, 5 for layer 4)
τ_L = all idx bits above e_L = which tree of layer L (τ₀ = 0: the cached top tree)
idx also selects the PORS instance (the tree field of its tweaks)
34 bits → 2³⁴ bottom leaves for a 2³² signing lifetime
one tree per idx · height 14 · 16,384 leaves · 15 opened leaves · forced pruning (octopus ≤ 120)
15 opened leaves (orange: secret from the witness) · 14 merges (dark dots) · 114 octopus nodes (rings)
Real example (idx = 11,956,472,188); x = leaf position / 16,384, tree drawn as a triangle.
Verifier = stack machine over the witness segments:
per leaf (increasing indices): leaf = Th(tw₉, s), then segments of a folds with witness nodes;
a merge pops the waiting left node (its heap index must match); 15 + 14 = 29 segments.
Accept iff folds ≤ 120, heap index 1 (root) and an empty stack: 29 + octopus ≤ 149 HASH calls
nodes: Th(tw₁₀(heap index) ‖ P ‖ left ‖ right); the octopus size is what the signer ground for.
w = 3 bits · 42 chains of 8 positions · digits must sum to 182 · no checksum chains
Enc(M, c) = H(tw₄ ‖ P ‖ M ‖ LE32 c): two 64-bit words, top bits 0,
21 + 21 digits x_i of 3 bits each; valid iff Σ x_i = 182 and c < 2²²
(the signer increments c until valid, ≈ 2,400 tries expected)
Verifier: steps x_i+1 … 7 (Th(tw₁, ·)), Σ(7 − x_i) = 294 − 182 = 112 per layer;
42 endpoints → leaf = Th(tw₂ ‖ P ‖ 42 × 16 B), a 704-byte HASH input
FIVE LAYERS FROM THE PORS ROOT TO THE PUBLIC KEY
Each layer: M_L + counter c_L → 42 digits → 42 chains → WOTS leaf → h folds → M_(L−1) = root of that XMSS tree

g.text: one height-14 tree of instance idx

svg.text: Orange: values carried by the witness. Blue: nodes the verifier recomputes. Real example path (idx = 11,956,472,188); layer 0 has τ₀ = 0.
KEYGEN CACHE: THE TOP TREE IS BUILT ONCE

g.text: keygen builds layer 0 (τ = 0, height 11) once and keeps all 4,094 nodes below the root in the K = 131,072-byte cache, masked and MAC-authenticated.
sign reads its layer-0 authentication path from the cache instead of rebuilding 2,048 WOTS leaves; verify never sees the cache.

svg.text: node (l, j), l = 0..10: byte 32 + 16 · (N_l + j), N_l = Σ_(k<l) 2^(11−k); the root (level 11) is not stored, it is pk
stored = X(l, j) ⊕ mask(l, j), mask(l, j) = Th(tw₁₃(l, j) ‖ P ‖ S): 16 B, a seed derivation like the WOTS / PORS secrets
tag = H(tw₁₄ ‖ P ‖ S ‖ region): the full 256-bit answer; 65,568-byte input = 1,025 blocks. A tampered cache fails the check (forgery chance 2⁻²⁵⁶ per request).

g.text: 1 build the top tree: 2,048 WOTS leaves + 2,047 nodes
2 4,094 masks; write X(l, j) ⊕ mask(l, j)
2 digest loop, PORS tree (16,384 leaves), layers 4…1
3 layer 0: counter c₀; leaf e₀ chains up to x_i only
layer 0 is checked like any layer:
siblings; a wrong sibling gives a root ≠ pk

svg.text: H(tw₀(lay, τ, k, e) ‖ P ‖ S)
PORS: H(tw₈(idx, q) ‖ P ‖ S) → leaves
Signer-side only: the verifier sees revealed secrets and chain values, never the PRF.
WITNESS EXPANSION: THE SEGMENT STREAM FOR THE STACK MACHINE

g.text: expand makes one hash (the digest), recomputes the leaf indices and the schedule, and rejects non-canonical signatures (indices not distinct, octopus > 120, nonzero unused slots).
W = 6,348 B; every 16-byte item is 8-aligned, so verify reads each with LD, and the stream tells the stack machine when to fold and when to merge.

svg.text: first 4 of the 29 segments of the example (stream at byte 272, not to scale): an 8-byte header, byte 0 = a | 16·merge | 32·t, then the a nodes n_i it folds (octopus read order)

g.text: π byte s = 8 × digest slot of the s-th smallest leaf; the verifier reads (π & 0x78) >> 3 (slot 15 = sentinel 2¹⁴) and requires strictly increasing indices
header: a ≤ 14 folds; t = bit 0 of the heap index where the segment starts (checked when a > 0); merge = pop the stack (its sibling heap index must match)

svg.text: layer L body (42 values + h_L siblings) at 2,424, 3,272, 4,040, 4,808, 5,576; counters c_L (LE32) at 6,328 + 4L; the witness is zero beyond W
Verify ≤ 9,784 + 17·folds + 2·(segments with folds) ≤ 11,882 cycles on every accepting run (proved; measured average 11,834) + ⌈6,348 / 256⌉ = 25 → C = 11,907.
Trees drawn schematically; real example paths, leaves and digits.
